transcript.text: Indesit dryer making a horrible squealing noise when it starts up, goes away after a few mins. Still dries fine

A squeal for the first few minutes, while it continues to dry, is most often the belt tension pulley (jockey/idler pulley) or belt becoming noisy when cold. As it warms slightly the noise can fade. A trapped item or fluff around the drum/filter area is also possible; worn drum supports are less likely unless it feels rough or rumbles by hand. 1. Switch off and unplug the dryer. Empty the drum, then check the drum lifters, lint filter and the filter slot for coins, hair grips, buttons or anything caught in the gap. Remove anything you can reach safely. This rules out the simple causes.
2. Still unplugged, turn the empty drum slowly by hand. If it squeaks or feels rough/rumbling, the drum support or belt-drive area needs attention. If it turns smooth and quiet, the idler pulley/belt is more likely because the fault only appears under running load. Avoid continuing to use it if the squeal becomes constant, turns into scraping/grinding, the drum struggles to turn, or there is a hot-rubber smell. If the drum is otherwise smooth and clear, an engineer can inspect the belt, tension pulley and drum supports; this normally involves dismantling the dryer rather than an owner repair.
Ok, I've checked the drum, lint filter and door seal and found nothing stuck. Turning the empty drum by hand (unplugged) it turns but has a slight squeak/scrape and feels a little rough.

The slight squeak/scrape and rough feel by hand mean this is unlikely to be a loose item. The most likely cause remains a worn jockey/idler pulley or belt, which commonly squeals when cold and quietens as it warms. However, the roughness also raises a worn drum support roller, bearing/bush or felt support. 1. With the dryer switched off, unplugged and empty, gently lift the front rim of the drum through the door opening — do not force it. Noticeable up-and-down play, a scrape as it lifts, or the drum sitting low points more towards a drum support/bearing or felt support problem. Little or no play points more towards the belt tension pulley/belt. Either way, this needs a dryer engineer to strip the cabinet and inspect the belt drive and drum supports; it is not sensible to identify or replace a part from the noise alone. Avoid using it if the squeal becomes continuous, changes to grinding, the drum starts struggling to turn, or there is any hot-rubber smell.

I'm not sure how to check that, I don't really know what I'm looking for when lifting the drum. I also can't tilt or lay the dryer down because of my back. Is there anything else I can check from the front?

Yes — there is one limited front-only check worth doing, and you do not need to lift or move the dryer. 1. Switch it off and unplug it. With the door open, shine a torch around the narrow gap between the front of the drum and the fixed front panel. Slowly turn the drum by hand and look for a felt strip/seal that is loose, folded over, badly frayed or visibly rubbing. Do not poke tools into the gap. • If you can see damaged or displaced felt, that would fit the slight scrape/roughness and needs an engineer to replace or refit the drum support/felt. • If it all looks even and intact, the cold-start squeal is more likely the belt tension pulley or belt inside the cabinet. Both require cabinet dismantling, so an engineer is the sensible next step rather than trying to tilt the machine yourself. Until then, it can usually be used cautiously only if the drum continues to turn normally and there is no burning-rubber smell, persistent grinding, or worsening noise. Stop using it if any of those appear.
Ok, I'll try the torch check, though I'm not sure I'll be able to tell if the felt looks right or not. If I can't tell, I'll just book an engineer.

That is a sensible plan. You do not need to judge minor cosmetic wear: only look for something obvious — a loose or folded flap of felt, a badly frayed section, or the drum visibly rubbing against the front panel as you turn it slowly by hand. If you cannot see an obvious problem, do not try to reach into the gap or move the dryer. A worn drum support/felt is the other realistic possibility. Both need the cabinet dismantled to confirm, so booking an engineer is the right next step. Describe it as: “Indesit tumble dryer squeals for the first few minutes, then quietens; the empty drum has a slight scrape/squeak and feels a little rough by hand.” Stop using it if the noise becomes constant or turns to grinding, the drum struggles, or there is a hot-rubber smell.

candidates: Jockey/idler pulley or belt tension system (high)
Foreign object or fluff in the drum/filter area (medium)
Drum support bearing or roller wear (low)
